# Phase 0 – Pre-fit observations and hypotheses

**Scope:** raw-data audit only (CLAUDE.md, Phase 0). No kinetic model fitted, no run excluded, no plant optimisation.
**Specification used:** `docs/assignment_brief.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (both read in full).
**Data:** `runs.csv` (8 runs), `timecourse.csv` (8 runs x 14 times, 0-48 h), `endpoint_hplc.csv` (8 rows). Raw files are unmodified (`data/raw/CHECKSUMS.sha256`).
**Sources of numbers:** `outputs/tables/*.csv`, generated by `src/phase0_inspect.py`. "sd" means the 1-sd measurement uncertainty given in brief section 3 (read in row order from a PDF-extracted table: biomass 3.5% + 0.08 g/L; TRS 1% + 0.4 g/L; ethanol 1.2% + 0.25 g/L; CO2 about 2%; glycerol/lactic about 3%; pH 0.04). Rates are finite differences between samples, **not model fits**.

Section A = what the data show. Section C = hypotheses (untested). Section B answers the brief's pre-fit question (Q1) as a prediction.

---

## A. Direct observations

### A1. Design and file structure
- **O1.** Design: 30 °C x {160, 220, 260 g/L} (R1-R3); 34 °C x {160, 220, 260} (R4-R6); R7 = repeat of R5; R8 = 37 °C, 220 g/L. Only one run is above 34 °C, and 37 °C is not crossed with any other sugar level.
- **O2.** No missing values, no duplicate rows or (run, time) keys. Run IDs R1-R8 match across files. Every run has exactly the brief's 14 time points. Sampling intervals widen from 2 h to 6 h after 24 h.
- **O3.** All concentration variables are in g/L (column names and brief). `lactic_acid_g_L` is a text column because of "n.d." (below 0.2 g/L per brief).

### A2. Initial conditions vs metadata (z in brief-sd units; |z| > 2 flagged)
- **O4.** t=0 TRS vs nominal: within 2 sd in 7 runs. R4 is 155.9 vs 160 (-2.56%, z = -2.09).
- **O5.** t=0 biomass vs 2.5 g/L inoculum: 2.2-2.92 g/L. Only R1 exceeds 2 sd (2.92, z = +2.31). R8 (2.2) is z = -1.9.
- **O6.** t=0 ethanol is 0.1-0.4 g/L in R3-R8 (0.0 in R1, R2); all within 2 sd of zero (sd 0.25). Cumulative CO2 is exactly 0 at t=0 in all runs.
- **O7.** TRS / "sucrose + reducing sugars" is 1.0367-1.0369 in all runs. This matches about 70% of the sugar mass being sucrose (inversion adds water, factor 1.0526 per g sucrose; implied fraction 0.697-0.702). The ratio is therefore chemically consistent, but the 70% figure is my inference, not stated in the brief.

### A3. Time-course behaviour
- **O8. Biomass.** About 2.5 -> 10-11.5 g/L by 24 h in all runs (24 h range 10.04-11.47), then roughly flat; 48 h range 10.87-12.33, with no clear relation to initial sugar (R1 11.18 at 160 g/L; R3 12.33 and R6 10.87 at 260 g/L). Decreases between samples reach 1.4 g/L; of all biomass decreases only R3 at 20 h (z = 2.64, OD600-based) and R4 at 42 h (z = 2.13) exceed 2 sd, so most of the scatter is consistent with the stated noise.
- **O9. Early ethanol rate (0-12 h average).** 2.84 and 2.88 g/L/h at 160 g/L; 2.53, 2.58, 2.61 at 220 g/L (R2, R5, R7); 2.47, 2.53 at 260 g/L; R8 (37 °C) 1.95. Measurement-only sd of such a rate is about 0.06 g/L/h, so the 160 vs 220/260 gap (~0.3) is ~3-4 sd and the R8 gap (~0.6) is ~8 sd. Run-to-run variation beyond measurement noise is not captured by those sds (see O18).
- **O10. Late slowdown with sugar remaining.** In R3, R6, R7 and R8, 28.6, 48.7, 28.7 and 49.4 g/L TRS remain at 48 h, while the sugar-uptake rate over 36-48 h has fallen to 50%, 34%, 31% and 43% of its 0-12 h value (R3 2.8, R6 2.0, R7 1.9, R8 1.8 g/L/h). R5 (6.6 g/L left) is similar in shape. Ethanol rate over 36-48 h is 0.6-1.4 g/L/h in the 220-260 g/L runs against 2.1-3.2 g/L/h over 12-24 h.
- **O11. 160 g/L runs.** R1 and R4 reach TRS 0.0 by 30 h and are nearly indistinguishable (30 vs 34 °C). Ethanol afterwards sits at 71.5-74.6 g/L.
- **O12. Temperature at 220 g/L (48 h).** R2 (30 °C): ethanol 100.5 g/L, TRS 0.0. R5 (34 °C): 96.6, 6.6. R8 (37 °C): 79.7, 49.4. At 24 h ethanol is 68.6 / 66.3 / 50.1.
- **O13. Temperature at 260 g/L.** R3 (30 °C): 107.8 g/L ethanol, 28.6 g/L TRS left. R6 (34 °C): 100.1 and 48.7. (R3 biomass is OD600-based.)
- **O14.** The highest ethanol is 107.8 g/L (R3, 48 h), still rising (36-48 h average 1.4 g/L/h). That is 13.7% v/v using the brief's 7.89 g/L per % v/v.
- **O15. Cumulative CO2** never decreases. In R1 (73.4 g/L) and R4 (70.0 g/L) it is identical at four consecutive samples from 30 h, when TRS is already 0.0. For an integrated off-gas flow this is what zero gas flow would give, but the CSV cannot confirm it.
- **O16.** 48 h ethanol:CO2 mass ratio is 0.978-1.066 (1:1 molar = 1.047). Only R1 (0.978, z = -2.8) is clearly off; the rest are within 1.4 sd.
- **O17.** Ethanol yield on TRS consumed (48 h ethanol / measured TRS drop) is 0.438-0.479 g/g, i.e. 86-94% of the 0.511 g/g theoretical (2 EtOH per glucose).
- **O18 (plant-relevant).** Only R1, R4 (TRS <= 5 g/L at 30 h) and R2 (42 h) reach the plant's 5 g/L end-of-batch limit within 48 h. R5 is at 6.6 g/L at 48 h, so its time to reach 5 g/L is beyond the data.

### A4. R5 vs R7 (same nominal conditions)
- **O19.** Similar to 12 h (ethanol 31.3 vs 31.7 g/L), then R7 falls behind: ethanol 40.1 vs 42.6 at 16 h, 56.4 vs 66.3 at 24 h, 84.2 vs 96.6 at 48 h. TRS at 48 h: 28.7 vs 6.6. Biomass at 48 h is the same within noise (0.4 sd).
- **O20.** In sd units, R5-R7 differences at 48 h are: TRS 26.6, ethanol 6.6, pH 9.9, glycerol 3.2 (R7 lower), biomass 0.4.
- **O21.** R7 is the only run with detectable lactic acid (9.00 g/L) and the only low final pH (3.84 vs 4.35-4.46, i.e. 14 sd below the median of the other runs).
- **O22.** The R5-R7 ethanol gap (12.4 g/L) is much larger than the 30 vs 34 °C gap at 220 g/L (R2 - R5 = 3.9 g/L).

### A5. Endpoint HPLC and pH (48 h)
- **O23.** Glycerol 7.35-10.99 g/L, generally higher at higher initial sugar (exceptions: R6 below R5; R7, R8 below R2/R5). Glycerol per g sugar consumed is 0.045-0.048 in all eight runs; glycerol/ethanol 0.096-0.106.
- **O24.** Lactic acid is n.d. (<0.2 g/L) in seven runs. Final pH 4.35-4.46 in seven runs (largest deviation from the median of the others: R6 +1.5 sd, R3 -1.3 sd).

### A6. Preliminary carbon balance (`preliminary_carbon_balance.csv`)
Carbon in = (measured t=0 TRS - 48 h TRS) x 0.400 g C/g glucose. Carbon out = ethanol + CO2 + glycerol + lactic + biomass gain (24.6 g per C-mol, i.e. 0.488 g C/g, from the brief). Constant volume; ethanol in the off-gas is returned (brief). Sd propagated from the brief sds.
- **O25.** Recovery (sd): R1 99.0 (1.7), R2 98.2 (1.6), R3 101.8 (1.8), R4 104.8 (1.8), R5 100.2 (1.7), R6 100.4 (1.9), R7 101.2 (1.8), R8 103.7 (2.1) %. All eight are within 3 sd of 100%; only R4 exceeds 2 sd (+2.6). Mean 101.2%, i.e. a possible small positive bias (mean z = +0.59 against an sd of the mean of about 0.35).
- **O26.** Ethanol + CO2 alone recover 86-93% of the carbon; glycerol and biomass supply most of the rest.
- **O27.** R7: with its 9 g/L lactic acid (3.6 g C/L) recovery is 101.2%; without it, 96.5% (z = -1.9). Lactic carbon is thus about 4.7% of the sugar carbon used.
- **O28.** Sensitivity: using nominal rather than measured t=0 TRS gives R4 102.1% (vs 104.8%) and R1 100.9% (vs 99.0%).
- **O29.** Carbon balance does not single out R3: it closes at 101.8%, so the carbon balance does not by itself argue against fitting R3. Its issue is the OD600 biomass method (biomass gain is about 5-7% of the carbon consumed).

---

## B. Pre-fit prediction for brief question 1
*"Which runs show that something other than running out of sugar stops the fermentation, and what do you think it is?"*

**Runs (from raw curves):** R8, R7, R6 and R3, with R5 a weaker case. They still contain 29-49 g/L TRS at 48 h (R5: 6.6) while uptake and ethanol rates have fallen to roughly 30-50% of their early values (O10).

**Candidate causes, by run** (all hypotheses):
- **R3, R6 (high sugar, ethanol 100-108 g/L):** ethanol toxicity, possibly combined with osmotic stress from the high initial sugar.
- **R8 (37 °C, ethanol only 80 g/L):** temperature stress, probably acting together with ethanol (ethanol tolerance falling with temperature). It cannot be ethanol alone, because R3 tolerates 108 g/L at 30 °C.
- **R7 (lactic acid 9 g/L, pH 3.84):** a second organism (lactic acid bacteria) competing for sugar and acidifying the broth. A yeast-only model may not apply to this run (decision for Level 1, not made here).

## C. Hypotheses (not tested; each needs model work and could be wrong)

| ID | Hypothesis | Motivated by | What would weaken it |
|----|-----------|--------------|----------------------|
| H1 | Ethanol inhibition slows growth and fermentation, and the ethanol level at which it bites falls with temperature. | O10, O12-O14 | Only one 37 °C run; R8 stalls at 80 g/L, R3 does not at 108 g/L, so a temperature-dependence is confounded with run-to-run effects. |
| H2 | Higher temperature is itself harmful (thermal stress) beyond its effect via ethanol. | O9, O12, O13 | The 30 vs 34 °C difference (3.9 g/L ethanol at 220) is smaller than the R5-R7 spread (O22). |
| H3 | High initial sugar (osmotic stress) lowers the early rate modestly. | O9: 2.8-2.9 vs 2.5 g/L/h, ~3-4 measurement sd | Differences are small; R5/R7 show other sources of variation. |
| H4 | Biomass levels off at 10-12 g/L because of a limiting non-sugar factor (e.g. nitrogen), not sugar or temperature. | O8 | No nutrient data in the files. |
| H5 | R7 had bacterial (lactic acid) contamination that diverted sugar and slowed the batch. | O19-O22, O27 | Lactic acid could also be a consequence of a slow, stressed fermentation; no microbiological data. |
| H6 | Loss of cell viability (not visible in dry weight) drives the late slowdown. | O8 vs O10: flat biomass with falling rates | No viability data. |
| H7 | The carbon recovery mean of 101.2% reflects a small systematic bias in one or more measurements (e.g. TRS or CO2), not a missing sink. | O25 | Only R4 exceeds 2 sd; a mean z of 0.59 is ~1.7 sd of the mean, so it could be chance. |
| H8 | Glycerol formation tracks sugar flux (constant 0.045-0.048 g per g sugar). | O23 | Endpoint values only. |

## D. Data-quality summary (`data_quality.csv`)
137 checks: 5 FLAG, rest PASS or INFO. The flags are R1 t=0 biomass, R4 t=0 TRS, R3 OD600 method, and two biomass dips (R3 at 20 h, R4 at 42 h). Two of 24 numeric t=0 comparisons (TRS, biomass, ethanol) and 2 of 22 step changes in the unexpected direction exceed 2 sd; noise alone would give about 1 of each at a 5% rate, so these are weak signals. No value has been changed.

## E. Uncertainties and items for later phases (not decisions)
1. **Not in the files:** initial pH, TRS detection limit, how the OD600 calibration for R3 was made and its uncertainty.
2. **CO2 plateau (R1, R4):** plausible as zero off-gas flow, not confirmable here.
3. **Uncertainty table mapping:** read in row order from extracted text; please confirm against the PDF.
4. **Run selection (CLAUDE.md rules 6 and 7):** no run is excluded in Phase 0. Whether to fit R3 (biomass series) and R7 (lactic acid, pH, divergence from R5) needs independent evidence in Level 1; the endpoint evidence in A4 and A6 is the starting point. The held-out run must be chosen and logged before any fitting or tuning. All eight raw curves have been viewed in Phase 0, which is allowed by the brief ("look at the raw curves"), but nothing here was tuned on any run.
5. **Plant-relevant coverage:** the data cover 30, 34 and 37 °C with a single 37 °C run (220 g/L) and no run at 33 or 36 °C. Questions about 37 °C at 260 g/L (brief Q5) and the 36 °C scenario would be extrapolations or interpolations to be flagged later (CLAUDE.md rule 10).
